title: 390. Flip Game II

examples.explanation: Flipping the middle pair leaves "+--+" with no reply.
No move exists for the first player.
Each possible first flip hands the opponent a winning board.

hints: A board is winning when some legal flip leads to a board that is losing for the player to move.
Boards with no flippable pair are losing; build up from there with memoised search.
Flipping splits the board into independent left and right parts, so identical substrings share results through memoisation.
